title: RADE: Learning Risk-Adjustable Driving Environment via Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion

control_signal.value: A scalar desired risk level r in [0.3, 1], a heuristic function of the scene's minimum Post-Encroachment Time (PET); a risk of 0.3 or more corresponds to PET below 1 s.

control_mechanism.value: Risk embedded by an MLP into a 128-dimensional latent, concatenated with the diffusion step embedding at every layer; trained with condition dropout and sampled with classifier-free guidance scale omega.

base_model.value: MADiff multi-agent diffusion: U-Net with multi-head attention on skip connections for cross-agent fusion, plus a tokenized dynamics check using a 1024-token motion vocabulary.

datasets.value: rounD roundabout dataset (two-lane roundabout, Neuweiler, Aachen); 0.4 s resolution, 3.2 s generation horizon.

metrics.value: Statistical realism (inter-vehicle distance, speed, yielding distance and speed distributions); PET distribution; crash rate across risk levels 0.3 to 1.0.

controllability_evidence.value: Mean crash rate rises from 20.6% to 50.6% as desired risk increases; PET below 0.4 s density rises 113%, from 0.030 to 0.064, from low to high risk.

notes: Validated on a single roundabout dataset; packet has no explicit limitations section.
